author: ttfreitas
text:
Hello, FX.Sniffer.

I have seen a few posts where you keep track of the COT indicators.

I saw this headline today published in my trading station and I was wondering if it matches your COT analysis.

CBA survey says Australian exporters expect AUD/USD to rise to 1.08 by the end of the year, importers expect AUD/USD at 1.11.

Cheers

author: FX.Sniffer
text:
Hi ttfreitas,

Here's the au COT

the commercial long contracts are increasing as you see from the chart till it reach level 100 where it will be at peak, but where it will take the price to?! there is no way to tell other than analyzing au's price chart.

Exporters & importers are a commercial traders and they hedge their international business transactions to maintain their planned profit margin in their base currency. So, the prices mentioned in the headline will effect their decision, but which are the majority in Australia.....exporters or importers ! You need an economist to research this. However I don't care about all of that, all I need is to monitor the two most significant levels in the COT chart to support my technical analysis.

BTW, the 1.08 is a nice supply area on the daily chart.

Cheers,

author: FX.Sniffer
text:
Cable; there is nothing interestig on LTF so by looking at daily we see a bullish move created a LQ gap preceeded by a failed inverted pinbar which is a sign of trapped sellers and an area where price tends to bounce from. On the upper side there is compression (multiple FTRs) and a flag limit where price might create a fakeout.

H4 and what to expect on it; price could drop from the current range to the trapped sellers area where we can buy targeting the higher levels, or price could rise to the fakeout area where we can sell targeting the lower level. Any significant price action other than what has been planned here could change the whole plan.
